text:
alex: Hey — quick sync: I'm proposing we simplify the rollout metadata surface. Current schema has ~8 optional fields and multiple tenant overrides. It's causing confusion in the resolver.

maya: +1 on simplification. can you sketch options?

alex: Three ideas: 1) Compact token encoding (binary TLV) that the control plane emits and clients decode. 2) Explicit verbose JSON per-tenant with full fields. 3) Hybrid: top-level compact hint + optional per-tenant verbose overrides. Each tradeoff: compact = efficient but opaque; verbose = debuggable but noisy; hybrid = more complexity in producer.

cheng: Concern: compact TLV makes debugging ops/alerts hard. We'd lose readable telemetry unless we add a decode step in the console.

sam: Hybrid seems pragmatic. We can keep the common rollout predicates in compact form and only expand when a tenant sets overrides. That keeps most traffic small.

rachel: How about graceful compat? Clients older than the decode lib should fallback to a 'compat string' that maps to a safe default model variant.

alex: Good. Proposal detail: enrich the compact header with a version byte + a stable key map. Example pseudo: ```hex
01 0A 02 04 // v1, TTL=10m, flags
04 <key-id> <payload>```

maya: Ops/observability asks: make sure console can auto-decode and surface both compact and expanded forms in the timeline. Otherwise runbooks will explode.

ops-bot: deploybot: noted. Added task INF-472 to enable runtime decode in canary console.

alex: Next action: I'll open a PR with the hybrid schema + compatibility rules, and a small golang/py decoder. Please review; aim for lightweight console decode first.

cheng: LGTM. Add a flag to control auto-expand in the API so we can flip it during rollout.

sam: Also add unit tests for resolver fallback when decode fails (corrupt/unknown version).

rachel: +1. Also document expected size savings with sample workloads (p50/p95). helps justify complexity.

alex: Thanks all — I'll post the PR link once ready. :thumbsup:
